transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SE), Martin Lee (Skybridge PM), Sofia Ramos (Skybridge Cloud Engineer), Diego Torres (Skybridge Marketplace)

Summary:
Quick technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for private deployments (VPC + partner-managed), and validation plan for joint reference-arch + marketplace listing. Agreed to next steps: share ref-arch draft, checklist, schedule SE benchmark session against a small workload in partner test tenant.

Topics:
- Marketplace listing metadata + billing/pricing templates
- Reference architecture (VPC peering vs Private deployment, KMS/HSM integration)
- E2E validation plan: benchmarks, security questionnaire, compliance docs
- Rollout plan & timelines for candidate customers

Transcript (timestamps approx, transcription imperfect in places):
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, let's do quick intros. I'm Alex, AE on the Redwood partners team. Priya's our SE, Jamal is here to help on the ref arch and benchmarks.
[00:12] Martin Lee: Hi all, Martin here, partner PM for Skybridge Cloud. Sofia and Diego are on from the product and engineering side.
[00:17] Sofia Ramos: Hello.
[00:20] Priya Patel: Awesome. Quick agenda, we wanted to run through the marketplace listing items, the reference architecture draft, and then the validation plan—benchmarks and security checks. Sound good?
[00:30] Diego Torres: Yep that's good. A couple of specific asks from our side: we need the listing copy, icons, pricing tiers, and any required docs for marketplace certification. Also, on the ref-arch, we want to know recommended network topology for private deployments.
[00:42] Alex Kim: Great, we'll walk through that. On marketplace we have a checklist — I'll upload the listing checklist and pricing template after the call. For the topology, Priya, do you want to run the high-level ref arch?
[00:53] Priya Patel: Sure. So the reference architecture we're proposing has two main patterns: hosted (Redwood hosted API with partner listing) and private (customer in partner VPC with Redwood Private control plane). For private we recommend either VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on partner controls; we also support an on-prem package if needed. There are tradeoffs around latency and data residency.
[01:15] Jamal Ortiz: Also, we'll include guidance on KV cache placement and batching config for common LLM workloads — that usually moves the needle on cost/latency.
[01:24] Martin Lee: When you say "private control plane" — can you clarify? We need to include exact network ports and KMS expectations for our marketplace docs.
[01:34] Priya Patel: Yeah, good call. For the Private deployment option we ship a customer-managed VPC connector; control plane can be either SaaS-managed with VPC peering or fully managed by the customer behind their firewall. KMS: we support customer KMS via standard KMS/HSM integrations, we can document key rotation and audit logs. I'll add the port list to the ref arch doc — it's in the draft already but we'll expand.
[01:55] Sofia Ramos: Are there any special compliance artifacts we need to surface for listing? SOC2, ISO?
[02:01] Alex Kim: We provide SOC2 attestation and can share redacted audit reports; for ISO let us know which cert you require, we can surface that via partner portal. Also we'll attach our data flow diagram to the listing package.
[02:12] Diego Torres: On pricing — do you have recommended pricing models for marketplace (per-inference vs committed capacity)? Skybridge would like to support both.
[02:21] Alex Kim: We typically offer two models: usage-based (per-token/per-embedding) for hosted, and reserved capacity for dedicated deployments. For marketplace listing we can include both options and a partner-managed billing pointer. I'll send a pricing template.
[02:33] Martin Lee: Great. On the validation side, we want to run a short benchmark (latency p95, throughput) against a sample workload. How do you recommend we provision test infra?
[02:44] Priya Patel: Ideally we get a read-only test tenant on Skybridge where Redwood SEs can run a few synthetic workloads. We'll focus on a 5k token/day scenario and a higher throughput chat scenario — measure p50/p95 latency, token cost, and fault tolerance under bursting. We also want to test KV cache hit rates.
[03:04] Sofia Ramos: We can provision a sandbox account, but we need the exact test plan. Can you share the script and traffic profile?
[03:11] Jamal Ortiz: We'll prepare a minimal workload script and spike/steady profiles. We'll post it to the shared folder and request access. Also, we'll include quantization profiles (int8) where applicable — note some partners require specific GPU families.
[03:28] Diego Torres: A question on images/containers — for on-prem we assume you'll provide a container image. Is that correct?
[03:35] Priya Patel: Yes for on-prem we provide a validated image and deployment guide. For private VPC connectors we use an agentless approach—no container on partner side unless they're doing full on-prem.
[03:45] Martin Lee: For the marketplace certification, is there a required support SLA?
[03:49] Alex Kim: For listings we recommend a minimum of business hours support for marketplace tier, but for Dedicated or enterprise we do SLA-backed support. We'll include suggested support levels in the checklist.
[03:58] Sofia Ramos: Security questionnaire — do you have a template we can fill?
[04:02] Alex Kim: Yes. We'll send our security questionnaire (SOC2 details, encryption at rest/in transit, logging/Audit log retention, RBAC/SSO) after the call. Martin, you said you'd prefer the docs inline in the marketplace listing?
[04:13] Martin Lee: We want them attached and also a short summary for the listing page.
[04:18] Priya Patel: Noted. We'll prepare a one-page security summary for the listing and attach the full questionnaire in the partner portal.
[04:25] Diego Torres: On billing integration — do you have existing marketplace connectors? We need a pointer to integrate billing events.
[04:32] Alex Kim: For a number of marketplaces we support a billing integration via webhook + reconciliation CSV export. We'll include sample payloads in the checklist. If Skybridge requires direct billing pass-through, we can discuss the integration details.
[04:44] Martin Lee: Okay. Back to ref arch details — can you speak to network egress expectations and where logs reside?
[04:50] Priya Patel: Logs can be pushed to partner-managed logging endpoints or stored in Redwood Console if the customer opts in. For private deployments logs stay in the customer VPC if they use the on-prem or dedicated mode. Egress depends on the chosen topology: with peering traffic stays internal, with public endpoints you need egress rules. We'll mark those in the diagram.
[05:08] Sofia Ramos: Any gotchas with KV cache and multi-tenant scenarios?
[05:11] Jamal Ortiz: For multi-tenant setups we recommend sharded KV cache per-tenant keys; avoid cross-tenant share to prevent leakage. We also document cache warming strategies to reduce cold-starts.
[05:22] Alex Kim: We should talk about rollout phases — initial listing + pilot customers then GA listing. What's Skybridge's timeline?
[05:28] Martin Lee: We'd like to get a pilot by mid-October and GA by end of November. That gives about six weeks for ref-arch docs and the marketplace cert. Is that feasible?
[05:36] Priya Patel: Yes that's feasible. We'll prioritize the ref-arch and checklist this week; SE benchmark session can be scheduled the week of 2026-09-28.
[05:45] Diego Torres: For the benchmark, do you need sample data or synthetic only?
[05:49] Jamal Ortiz: Synthetic is fine for latency; for accuracy/regression tests we'll need redacted sample prompts. If you can provide a small set, that helps.
[05:58] Sofia Ramos: We'll prepare a redacted prompt set and share via secure link.
[06:02] Alex Kim: Great. A couple of small items: icon and marketing assets — Diego, can you share the preferred sizes and any compliance copy?
[06:10] Diego Torres: We'll send asset specs after the call.
[06:13] Priya Patel: We'll also note recommended quantization and model variants for common workloads — e.g., 8-bit quantization for cost-sensitive batch workloads, fp16 for latency-sensitive production.
[06:25] Martin Lee: One more question: do you have any regional constraints? Some of our customers require EU-only data residency.
[06:31] Alex Kim: Yes we support region pinning — Redwood Dedicated in EU regions and Private deployments that keep data in EU. We'll document the process for region pinning and KMS regional keys.
[06:40] Diego Torres: Cool.
[06:42] (longer discussion on topology specifics, ports, and KMS integration — transcript abbreviated)
[15:00] Priya Patel: (reading from the ref-arch doc) Port list: 443 for control plane, 5222 for... uh, sorry that's a typo, it's 5222 only if you're using legacy messaging — most customers just use 443 and the agent uses outbound TLS. We'll tidy this.
[15:20] Sofia Ramos: Noted.
[18:10] Martin Lee: Security: can you confirm encryption at rest is customer-managed when using KMS?
[18:15] Alex Kim: Correct — when KMS is supplied by customer it controls the envelope keys; Redwood's storage uses envelope encryption with that KMS. We'll add explicit steps under the key rotation section.
[22:00] Jamal Ortiz: On benchmarks: we'll capture p50/p95 latency, token cost, and e2e error rates. SEs will run small burst and steady-state tests.
[26:42] Sofia Ramos: Action: we'll create a sandbox account, but we need to know IP allowlist ranges for the Redwood SE run.
[26:51] Priya Patel: We'll provide the IP ranges in the ref-arch doc and also can use temporary SSH bastion if needed for private tests.
[30:00] Diego Torres: Marketplace listing — what's the approval cadence? How long does cert usually take?
[30:07] Alex Kim: It depends on marketplace. Typically if docs are complete and security questionnaire is answered, certification is 1-2 weeks. If integration requires deeper validation (billing, infra) it can be longer. We should aim for pilot mid-October as discussed.
[35:20] (few clarifying Q&A on billing payloads and partner portal access)
[40:00] Alex Kim: Recap: Priya to share ref-arch draft + port list by 2026-09-29; Alex will send listing checklist + pricing template by 2026-09-24; Martin will return security questionnaire by 2026-10-01; SEs to schedule benchmark week of 2026-09-28. We'll also get asset specs and sandbox details.
[40:25] Martin Lee: Sounds good.
[40:30] Sofia Ramos: Thanks everyone.
[40:33] Alex Kim: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with the links.

References / shared artifacts mentioned:
- Ref-arch draft (will be updated): https://redwood.ai/partners/skybridge/ref-arch-draft (note: placeholder link)
- Marketplace listing checklist & pricing template (to be uploaded)
- Security questionnaire (to be shared after call)
